2. Facts in short are that the opposite parties as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 85 of 1998 for partition and the suit was decreed in part on 16-3-2004 for 5.10 decimals land and defendant No. 1 got saham for 27.90 decimals. Against above judgment and decree defendant No. 1 preferred Title Appeal No. 125 of 2004 and the same was decreed on compromise on 20.4.2010. 

 10. It is admitted that the petitioners filed a petition under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for being added as defendants in the partition suit before the drawing of final decree. It is also admitted that the predecessors of the petitioner's were defendant's No. 4-5 and 9-14 in the above suit but they did not contest the suit but sold their 24.75 decimal to the petitioners by a registered kobla deed on 29-7-2010 during pendency of above suit. 

 11. In a suit for partition only co-shares of the disputed joma are made parties. Since the predecessors of the petitioner were impleaded as defendants in the suit they were co-shares and they had subsisting interest in the joma. Above defendants sold their land to the petitioners by a registered kobla deed on 29-7-2020. As such the petitioners have stepped in to the shoe of above defendants and they have locus standi to be impleaded in the above suit in the place of defendant's No. 4-5 since 9-14 since the suit for partition has not been disposed of finally by drawing up a final decree. The petitioners did not claim any property from opposite parties nor the opposite parties claim property of defendants No. 4-5 of 9-15. 

 13. Defendant Nos. 4, 5 and 9-14 did not contest the suit and now after transferring their land they must not have any interest to contest above suit. Since the suit is for partition and the same has been decreed in preliminary form the petitioners will be bound by the decree. If their petition under Order I, rules 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is allowed and they are made a party to the suit. They may be entitled to a saham but without affecting the preliminary decree. 

 14. The learned Additional District Judge should have allowed the revision since the suit is still pending in the trial court to avoid multiplicity of suits and enable the petitioners to get separate saham for their land, if any without affecting the preliminary decree but the learned Additional District Judge failed to do so and most illegally rejected the revision and affirmed the flawed order of the learned Assistant Judge which is not tenable in law.
